invalid_failure_risks: The canonical flow identity and the exact deterministic tie-breaking rule for ambiguous candidate assignments are not stated explicitly; relying only on a hidden reference can make a reasonable implementation appear incorrect.
The oracle protocol may be difficult to characterize reliably if the executable has undocumented timing, buffering, or reset behavior, especially under a 1 CPU and 2 GB limit.

The stated 99.5% row threshold and 1% byte-error allowance may mask serious per-route errors, while the text also says every physical packet must be counted exactly once; the acceptance policy should define which requirement takes precedence.
It is unclear whether the solver receives the generator, reference outputs, or only the visible spools, making the requested validation workflow potentially unavailable.
The offline test could falsely fail if it treats the permitted local UNIX-socket oracle interaction as network access or if unrelated startup behavior performs name resolution.
No execution-time or output-ordering specification is given, so a correct implementation could fail due to resource exhaustion or nondeterministic row ordering rather than logic.
review.reasons: The task has a concrete deployment target, deterministic verification inputs, and several independent hidden behaviors that defeat shallow fixes. The likely solution requires substantially more than the roughly 20-command source-inspection speedrun, although the opaque oracle and constrained matching make solvability borderline under the stated time and resource limits.
fixes: Define canonical packet identity and the exact tie-breaking behavior for globally ambiguous but otherwise valid assignments in the task materials or verifier contract.
State whether the solver may use or inspect the generator and reference harness, and provide a local deterministic fixture generator if it is expected to perform those checks.
Clarify how the 99.5% row threshold relates to the absolute exactly-once and route-permission requirements.
Specify deterministic output row ordering and add explicit resource and runtime limits to the verifier.
Make the offline test distinguish forbidden external networking from the required local UNIX-socket routeoracle connection.
